writeup.headline: Revvity rates Hold: strong momentum and solid cash generation offset by slowing growth and a full valuation.
writeup.thesis: Revvity scores 53, a Hold, because a very strong price trend and good quality are balanced by weak growth, valuation and balance sheet scores. The trend factor scores 100: the price is at its 52-week high, 48.4% above its 200-day average, with shares 92.1 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days. Quality scores 75 on a 19.2% FCF margin, a 12.3% operating margin, low stock-based pay and diluted share count down 5.0% year on year. Growth scores only 30, with TTM revenue growth of 4.0% and latest-quarter revenue growth of 1.3% year on year, as growth slowed by 5.7 pp from the previous quarter. Valuation scores 23: in absolute terms the multiples are high (6.3x sales, 33.1x FCF, 57.5x EBIT, FCF yield 2.0 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield), and the stock is expensive against its own history, for example more expensive than at 59 of the last 61 month-ends on P/S.
key_risks: Revenue growth is slowing, with latest-quarter growth of 1.3% year on year.
Valuation is high in absolute terms and expensive against its own history, leaving little room for disappointment.
After a sharp run to its 52-week high, the share price could give back gains if momentum fades.
Net debt is 3.94x free cash flow, with cash covering only 0.32 of debt.
Q3 results on 2026-11-03 could reset expectations around the raised full-year guidance.
what_would_change: A move to Buy needs 12 more points, most plausibly from growth re-accelerating or the valuation score improving as multiples fall or earnings rise.
A drop to Sell needs a loss of 9 points, such as the trend score falling from 100 if the rally reverses.
A guidance cut or weaker Q3 results would pressure the growth and news scores.
Debt reduction that lowers net debt to FCF would lift the balance sheet score.
